title: Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office Headquarters — Former Administration Building Renovation
size: Adaptive reuse of the former Forsyth County Administration Building at 110 E. Main St. into the future Sheriff’s Office headquarters
developer: Forsyth County / Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office
timing: Fresh local reporting shows the former Administration Building fenced for active construction and conversion into the future Sheriff’s Office headquarters as of early September 2026. Because work is already mobilized, the best contractor play is to identify the active GC and pursue remaining MEP, low-voltage, security/access-control, interiors, specialty equipment and closeout packages.
source: Forsyth County News — future Sheriff’s Office headquarters at former Administration Building

title: GA 400 Center — $10M Office Campus Repositioning
size: 430,046 SF, three-building office campus; approximately $10M refresh program
developer: Third & Urban with Zalik Investment Group
timing: Third & Urban has completed new roofs and chillers and begun construction on an outdoor courtyard and elevated tenant amenity lounge; lobby refreshes across all three buildings began in summer 2026. Seven new tenants plus renewals/expansions create additional TI activity. Contractors should target property management, leasing and active project teams for lobby, amenity, MEP, glazing, controls and tenant-fit-out packages.
source: CityBiz / Rough Draft / AJC reporting on Third & Urban capital improvements

title: North Point Mall — Sports & Entertainment District Redevelopment
size: ~99 acres; 20,000-seat arena, 1,385 apartments, 750,000 SF office, 565,000 SF commercial, 650 hotel rooms, community ice rink, cinema and structured parking
timing: Alpharetta City Council approved the rezoning 4-3 on August 24, 2026. The entitlement clears a major land-use hurdle, but an NHL franchise, financing and detailed construction sequencing remain unresolved; public reporting indicates meaningful demolition/construction may be a year or more away. Treat this as an early prequalification and relationship-building target with Jamestown and future CM/GC teams rather than a current bid.
source: Atlanta Journal-Constitution / Atlanta News First — Alpharetta rezoning approval
